locator.value: C6 — totals, averages and simple interest. Page 5 Example 3 defines P,t,r; P(1+rt); f(t) dollars/year; 1000/month to 12000/year; Δt=1/12 and t_i=i/12. Page 6 forms each principal contribution f(t_i)Δt, twelve-term total, its integral, each loan's remaining-interest factor and total debt integral. Notes lines 207–295 teach mean-value construction, rate-to-total dimensions, monthly sum, refinement with n changed, and the complete loan-to-weight-to-integral model. Original symbol t as elapsed loan age is mapped to τ before t denotes borrowing calendar time. The condition r≥0 is represented by the actual 6% examples; no negative-rate model is silently used. Simple versus compound interest, continuous versus twelve actual month-end loans, no fees/repayments and settlement time are explicit. Generated constant examples and Q5's increasing f(t) supply connected calculation and timing discrimination; generalized T−t expression retains the source's convention. The source's initial mention of averages is not omitted: notes lines 207–213 construct the constant-equivalent average, and Q6 applies both signed and magnitude averages.
